root_cause: The PostgreSQL data directory filesystem (80 MB) filled up during a large INSERT, so Postgres could not extend its data files.
The Redis data directory (6 MB) filled up, so Redis could not write its append-only file (AOF).
The filesystem holding the nginx access log (300 KB) filled up, so nginx could not write log lines.
The export job's /data filesystem (3 MB) filled up and every batch write failed with ENOSPC.
The container's DNS server points at a host that runs no DNS server, so example.com cannot be resolved and uploads fail.
The container's DNS server points at a host that runs no DNS server, so the sync worker cannot resolve example.com.
resolv.conf points at 127.0.0.1 where no DNS server runs, so the database host name cannot be resolved.
The nginx resolver directive points at a host that runs no DNS server, so the upstream host example.com cannot be resolved.
The worker exits at start because the DATABASE_URL environment variable is missing; supervisord restarts it until it gives up.
The app exits at start because the Python module requests_oauthlib is not installed; supervisord restarts it until it gives up.
The render worker segfaults (SIGSEGV) right after starting; supervisord restarts it until it gives up.
The API exits at start because /etc/api/config.json does not exist; Docker's restart policy restarts it 5 times.
The nginx web root /usr/share/nginx/html is mode 700 (root only), so nginx workers get Permission denied on every file.
The billing service runs as uid 1000 but /var/log/app is not writable by it, so opening its log file fails with Permission denied.
Postgres runs as uid 70 but its PGDATA parent directory is owned by root, so initdb cannot create the data directory.
The export job runs as user web but /srv/uploads is read-only (mode 555), so writing the report fails with Permission denied.
A stray nginx instance started earlier already listens on port 80, so the new nginx cannot bind 0.0.0.0:80 and exits.
A first redis-server already listens on port 6379, so the second redis-server cannot bind and aborts.
Another PostgreSQL in the same network namespace already listens on port 5432, so this one cannot bind and exits.
The metrics server already listens on port 8000, so orders-api cannot bind port 8000.
The report builder keeps growing in memory until the container's 96 MB limit is reached and the kernel OOM-kills it.
The report builder exceeds the 250 MB virtual memory limit (ulimit -v) and Python raises MemoryError.
Redis reached its maxmemory (3 MB) with the noeviction policy, so writes fail with OOM command not allowed.
The Node.js cache warmer exceeds its 48 MB heap limit (--max-old-space-size) and crashes with JavaScript heap out of memory.
The nginx config has a typo, 'listn' instead of 'listen', so nginx refuses to start.
redis.conf has an invalid maxmemory value ('512mbx'), so Redis refuses to start.
PostgreSQL is started with an invalid value for shared_buffers ('lots'), so it refuses to start.
One host is guessing the root password over SSH, with many failed logins in a short time.
One host is trying many invalid user names over SSH (user enumeration / password guessing).
Three hosts are guessing root and common user passwords over SSH at the same time.
